content: The metabolism of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may be reduced when co-administered with certain drugs, leading to increased levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Caution and close monitoring are advised in these cases. Below are specific interactions and recommendations: 1. Repaglinide: Co-administration with glecaprevir/pibrentasvir can increase the levels or effects of both drugs due to reduced metabolism. Monitor closely and use caution. 2. BCRP Inhibitors: Drugs that inhibit BCRP (breast cancer resistance protein) may increase plasma concentrations of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Use caution and monitor for toxicities. 3. OATP1B1/OATP1B3 Inhibitors: These inhibitors can increase the plasma concentration of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir. Monitor closely and adjust therapy as needed. 4. Rifabutin: This drug decreases the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely, as therapeutic efficacy may be reduced. 5. Rifaximin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases rifaximin levels via P-glycoprotein (P-gp) inhibition. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 7. Rosuvastatin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir increases rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting OATP1B1. This may increase the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis.
